answers.d01: 只懂高中概率也能讲清似然。抛一枚硬币 10 次得 7 次正面。现在固定这批数据，比较不同假设：若硬币均匀（正面概率 0.5），出现这个结果的概率是 C(10,7)×0.5¹⁰ ≈ 0.117；若正面概率是 0.7，则是 C(10,7)×0.7⁷×0.3³ ≈ 0.267。这两个数就是似然：给定参数，这批数据出现的机会。它回答的问题是「哪个假设更配得上这批数据」，这里 0.7 的假设胜出。后验概率则反过来回答「看过数据之后，这个假设本身有多可信」。两者的桥梁是贝叶斯公式：后验 ∝ 似然 × 先验。也就是说，似然只比较各假设对数据的解释力；要得到后验，还得乘上数据到来前你对各假设的信念（先验），再归一化。别混淆：似然大不等于该假设就可信，有限数据提供的证据有限，先验和备择假设都在起作用。
answers.d02: You know the average: heights 170, 170, 170 and 150, 170, 190 both average 170, yet the second group clearly varies more. Variance captures that. Take each value's distance from the mean: 0, 0, 0 versus -20, 0, +20. Distances below the mean are negative, and simply adding them cancels to zero, hiding all spread — so we square each distance: 400, 0, 400. The average of these squared distances, 800/3 ≈ 267, is the population variance; we divide by N, the whole group's size, because every member counts equally. Squaring also makes big deviations dominate: one person 40 off matters far more than two people 20 off. The unit becomes cm², awkward for talking, so we usually take the square root — the standard deviation, back in centimeters. Rule of thumb: variance near zero means values hug the mean; large variance means they scatter widely.
answers.d03: 麦克风凑近音箱，一声轻微的啸叫几秒内变成刺耳强音——这就是正反馈。机制是：输出的一部分被送回输入端，且方向与原变化相同。声音变大→拾进麦克风的声音变大→放大后输出更大→再拾回去更大，绕一圈放大一次，变化像滚雪球。注意它放大的是「变化的方向」，不是「价值」：股市恐慌时，下跌引发抛售，抛售加剧下跌，这条链路不关心跌得该不该。所以正反馈是好事还是坏事，取决于被放大的变化本身：群体免疫是良性循环，谣言传播则是恶性循环。放大也不是无限的——音箱功率、可用资金总有上限，增幅会递减甚至崩溃。判别要点：只要回路里「结果反过来加强原因」，就是正反馈；想让它停下，就切断回路中的某一环。
answers.d04: You have a free Saturday afternoon: the options are nap, gym, or helping a friend move. Opportunity cost is the value of the single best option you give up — not all of them. If you choose the gym, the cost isn't 'napping AND moving'; you could only have done one of the others anyway, so the cost is whichever of those you'd realistically have done — say, the nap. This is why 'free' things aren't free: the afternoon costs no money, yet picking a cheap movie still costs you the afternoon's best alternative. It also explains why high earners pay for errands: two hours of chores at $20/hour of value costs them roughly $100 of foregone earnings. Practical rule: for any choice, ask 'what is the next-best thing I'm giving up?' — if that alternative is worth more than the choice itself, switch.
answers.d05: 某病患病率 1%，检测对患者的阳性率 99%，对健康人的误报率 5%。你检出阳性，患病概率是多少？直觉说 99%，但先要考虑基数：人群里健康人是患者的 99 倍。设总人数 10000：患者 100 人，其中 99 人检出阳性；健康人 9900 人，5% 即 495 人被误报。阳性共 99 + 495 = 594 人，真患者只有 99 人，所以 P(患病|阳性) = 99/594 ≈ 16.7%。贝叶斯公式做的就是这次换算：P(患病|阳性) = P(阳性|患病)×P(患病)/P(阳性)。分子是「患病且检出阳性」的占比，分母是「所有检出阳性」的占比。关键是别把「患病的人有多大几率阳性」当成「阳性的人有多大几率患病」——条件方向相反，是两个不同的问题。患病率越低，误报在阳性中占比越大，阳性结果越要打折看待。
answers.d06: A cache keeps a copy of data close by so you don't recompute or re-fetch it — like taping a photocopied menu to your fridge instead of calling the restaurant each time. Cache invalidation is deciding when that copy is stale and must be thrown away. The problem: the moment the real data changes, your copy silently becomes wrong. A product page cached for an hour shows the old price until it expires, and nothing alerts you. Two broad strategies: time-to-live — the copy expires after, say, 60 seconds; simple, but you serve stale data within the window. Or explicit invalidation — when the price updates, actively delete the cached page; fresh, but you must catch every place the data is used, and one missed spot keeps serving a stale copy indefinitely. That's why it's called one of the hard problems: the cache never knows on its own that the source changed.
answers.d07: 冰淇淋销量与溺水人数同涨同跌，相关性很强，但冰淇淋不会让人溺水——共同原因是夏天：天热既让人多吃冰淇淋，也让人多下水。这就是「相关不等于因果」的典型结构：A 与 B 一起变化，可能是 A 导致 B，可能是 B 导致 A，也可能两者同受第三个因素 C 驱动，甚至纯属巧合。判断因果要回答的是：如果主动改变 A，B 会跟着变吗？单纯的观察数据回答不了，因为买冰淇淋的人和不买的人本来就不同（天热程度、游泳习惯都不同）。随机对照试验能解决：随机分组让两组人其他条件大致相同，只在冰淇淋上不同，再看溺水率是否变化。实际中看到相关时，先列出候选的混杂因素，问研究有没有控制它们；在没有控制之前，把相关直接读成因果都可能出错。
answers.d08: Compound growth means growth applied to a growing base: each period's gain is added on and earns too. $1,000 at 10% per year: $1,100, then $1,210, then $1,331 — the yearly gain grows from $100 to $110 to $121 because last year's interest itself earns interest. After n years the value is 1000 × 1.1ⁿ; the exponent is why growth accelerates: 20 years gives about $6,700, not the simple-interest $3,000. Why the starting amount matters: it sits in front of the same multiplier. Starting with $2,000 at the identical rate yields exactly double at every point — about $13,400 after 20 years — because multiplication scales everything equally. Time is the starting amount's twin: investing $1,000 at 25 versus $1,000 at 35, same rate, leaves the early starter with 1.1¹⁰ ≈ 2.6 times more, purely from ten extra years of compounding.
answers.v01: 你让学生备考：如果只让他背下每道练习题的答案，遇到原题满分，换一道新题就不会——这就是过拟合。机器学习同样如此：模型在训练数据上记住了细节和噪音（比如「手机尾号是 8 的用户都不流失」这类偶然规律），而不是真正有用的规律（比如「常投诉的用户更易流失」）。结果训练集准确率很高，一到没见过的新数据就掉下来。怎么发现？留一部分数据不参与训练，用作验证集：训练集成绩涨、验证集成绩跌，就是过拟合的信号。怎么办？换更简单的模型、要求规律更平滑、或补充更多数据——好比不让学生死记硬背，而是讲透原理。但也别矫枉过正：模型太简单会连真规律都学不到，那是另一个错误（欠拟合）。目标从来不是训练集分数，而是对新数据的预测。
answers.v02: Search for 'jaguar photos' and the engine returns 10 results: 6 are actual jaguar images, 4 are car pictures. Precision asks: of what was returned, how much is right? 6/10 = 60%. It measures false alarms — every car picture wasted your attention. Suppose the database holds 20 real jaguar photos but the search found only 6. Recall asks: of what exists, how much was found? 6/20 = 30%. It measures misses. The two can pull apart: returning only the single most certain result gives 100% precision but terrible recall; returning everything gives 100% recall but terrible precision. Which matters more depends on the task — spam filters tolerate few false alarms (precision), cancer screening tolerates few misses (recall). Both are computed from the same results; they just divide by different totals: what was returned versus all relevant items.
answers.v03: 浅色地衣上的灰色蛾子：深色个体更常被鸟吃掉，留下后代少；浅色个体存活多，后代里「浅色」占比升高。几十代后种群整体变浅——这就是自然选择改变种群的方式。关键在于：蛾子没有努力变浅，也没有任何个体在过程中变色。变异在出生时已经随机存在，环境只做筛选，让某些个体留下更多后代；变化发生在代际之间种群的比例上，而非个体自身。所以别把进化想成「长颈鹿为够到高处的叶子把脖子拉长」：真实过程是脖子本来就长短不一，矮处叶子先被吃光时，脖子长的饿死少、繁殖多，长脖基因在种群中的占比一代代上升。变异提供原料，选择做筛选，遗传把结果传下去；方向由环境决定，没有任何个体带着意图在努力。
answers.v04: An operation is idempotent if doing it once and doing it five times leave the system in the same state. 'Set user status to inactive' is idempotent; 'subtract $10 from the balance' is not — five calls remove $50. Why care in distributed systems? Networks fail unpredictably: you send a payment request, the timeout fires, and you don't know whether the server processed it. Retrying is the natural response, but for non-idempotent operations a retry can double-charge. The standard fix is an idempotency key: the client generates a unique ID per logical request and sends it with every retry; the server remembers completed keys and returns the original result instead of executing again. Compare: GET is naturally idempotent; DELETE by ID is idempotent because the second call changes nothing; POST 'create order' is not, unless you add such a key.
answers.v05: 猜一枚硬币：正反各半时最拿不准；两面几乎都是正面时你基本稳赢。信息熵就是把这种「平均拿不准的程度」算成一个数。对每种结果的概率 p，算 −log₂p，再按概率加权求和。概率小时 log 值大，意思是罕见结果一旦出现信息冲击大；加权让常见结果主导平均值。均匀分布为何最不确定？两个结果的例子：概率 0.9/0.1 时，熵 = −0.9log₂0.9 − 0.1log₂0.1 ≈ 0.14 + 0.33 = 0.47 比特；改成 0.5/0.5 时，0.5×1 + 0.5×1 = 1 比特。只要概率偏斜，一边变得「几乎确定」，不确定性就被压低；对称的 0.5/0.5 没有任何偏向可供利用，熵达到上限。所以熵衡量的是平均猜测难度，不是某个具体结果单独的意外程度。
answers.v06: Two processes, two resources. Process A holds the printer and asks for the file lock; process B holds the file lock and asks for the printer. Each waits for the other, neither releases what it holds, and both wait forever — that's deadlock. Four conditions must hold simultaneously: mutual exclusion (a resource serves one holder at a time), hold-and-wait (a process keeps its resources while waiting for more), no preemption (resources can't be forcibly taken away), and circular wait (A waits for B, B waits for A). Breaking any one condition prevents deadlock; in practice the easiest is a global ordering on resources — every process must request locks in the same order, say printer before file — which makes circular wait impossible. Databases take another route: they detect the wait cycle and kill one victim transaction so the rest can proceed.
answers.v07: 路灯是典型的公共物品：多一个人走路用它，不会减少别人能用的光（不竞争）；也没法只让付过钱的人照明、把路人挡在黑暗里（难排他）。这两个性质带来一个麻烦——既然不付钱也能享受，很多人就选择不付，等着别人出钱，这叫搭便车。村庄集资装路灯，人人都受益，但每个人都想：「我少出一份，灯多半还是会装，我省下钱还能白用光。」人人这么算，灯就装不起来，所有人都受损失。所以市场会少提供公共物品，路灯、国防、防洪堤通常要靠税收来建。判断要点是问两件事：用起来会不会互相挤占？能不能把没付钱的人挡在外面？两个答案都是否，就容易搭便车，需要集体分摊的安排。
answers.v08: Little's law says: in a stable system, the average number of items inside (L) equals the arrival rate (λ) times the average time each item spends inside (W): L = λW. Suppose 20 customers per hour enter a coffee shop and each spends 6 minutes (0.1 hour) from joining the line to leaving with coffee. Then on average 20 × 0.1 = 2 people are inside at any moment. It sounds obvious but is remarkably general: it holds for any queue discipline — first-come-first-served, priorities, even chaos — as long as you use long-run averages and the system is stable, meaning arrivals don't exceed capacity so the line doesn't grow without bound. Two practical uses: measure any two quantities and predict the third — if 100 requests per second hit a server and each spends 50 ms inside, expect 100 × 0.05 = 5 requests in flight on average; or infer hard-to-measure time from easy-to-count arrivals and occupancy.
